name: Kansas City
operatingHours: The KC Streetcar runs from Berkley Riverfront through the River Market, downtown and Union Station down Main Street to the Plaza and UMKC, 5:00 AM–midnight Sun–Thu and 5:00 AM–1:00 AM Fri–Sat, every ~10–15 min (less often early, late and on weekends).
fareInfo: The KC Streetcar is free to ride (no ticket needed). RideKC buses resumed fares on 1 June 2026: $2 a ride, $4 day pass, $20 weekly, paid by contactless card tap (no Amex) or the RideKCGO app.

sights.name: National WWI Museum and Memorial
sights.note: America's official World War I museum, entered over a glass bridge above a field of poppies; the Liberty Memorial tower's deck (small fee) gives a top skyline view.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, closed Tue (open daily Memorial Day–Labor Day)

sights.name: The Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art
sights.note: Encyclopedic art museum with standout Asian galleries and the Bloch Building's glass lenses; the lawn sculpture park is famous for its giant shuttlecocks. Free entry.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM Sat–Mon, 10:00 AM–9:00 PM Thu–Fri, closed Tue–Wed; sculpture park sunrise–sunset

sights.name: Arabia Steamboat Museum
sights.note: Cargo of a steamboat that sank in the Missouri River in 1856, dug out of a Kansas cornfield in 1988 and shown in astonishing condition, from pickles to boots.

sights.name: Union Station
sights.note: Restored 1914 Beaux-Arts station with a vast Grand Hall, still served by Amtrak and home to Science City, a planetarium, exhibits and restaurants.
sights.hours: Building ~6:00 AM–midnight daily; attractions have their own hours

sights.name: Country Club Plaza
sights.note: 1920s Spanish-style shopping district laid out around fountains and tiled towers, lit up with holiday lights from Thanksgiving to mid-January.
sights.hours: Shops ~10:00 AM–8:00 PM Mon–Sat, ~12:00–6:00 PM Sun; restaurants later

sights.name: Kansas City Zoo & Aquarium
sights.note: Large zoo in Swope Park with African savanna and Australia zones, a penguin house and a newer aquarium; well off the streetcar, so drive or ride-share.
sights.hours: 9:30 AM–4:00 PM daily Nov–Feb; Mar–Oct 9:30 AM–4:00 PM Mon–Fri, to 5:00 PM Sat–Sun

sights.name: Kauffman Stadium
sights.note: The Royals' 1973 ballpark, known for the crown scoreboard and the water-spectacular fountains beyond the outfield; 13 km east of downtown at the Truman Sports Complex.
sights.hours: Game days (Apr–Sep); stadium tours on select dates

sights.name: Negro Leagues Baseball Museum
sights.note: Moving history of Black professional baseball in the 18th & Vine Jazz District, ending on a 'Field of Legends' of bronze players; shares a building with the American Jazz Museum.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM Tue–Sat, 12:00–5:00 PM Sun, closed Mon

sights.name: The National Museum of Toys and Miniatures
sights.note: Huge collection of antique toys and museum-grade fine-scale miniatures on the UMKC campus, a short walk from the streetcar's UMKC terminus.

sights.name: GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium
sights.note: Home of the Chiefs and one of the NFL's loudest stadiums; tailgating in the lots is part of the ritual. Next to Kauffman Stadium, far east of the centre.
sights.hours: NFL game days (Sep–Jan); stadium tours on select dates

sights.name: Hallmark Visitors Center
sights.note: Free exhibits at Hallmark's Crown Center headquarters on the card company's history and printing, next door to the free Kaleidoscope kids' art studio.

sights.name: City Market
sights.note: River Market's open-air market square with a year-round weekend farmers market, plus delis, spice shops and global eateries open daily.
sights.hours: Farmers market Sat–Sun 8:00 AM–3:00 PM (Apr–Oct), 9:00 AM–3:00 PM in winter (Sat only Jan–Feb); shops daily

sights.name: The Money Museum
sights.note: Free museum at the Federal Reserve Bank with a window onto the cash-processing vault, a 27-pound gold bar and a bag of shredded money to take home. Photo ID required.
sights.hours: 9:30 AM–4:00 PM Mon–Fri (last entry 3:30 PM), closed weekends and bank holidays

sights.name: Boulevard Brewing Company
sights.note: Kansas City's flagship craft brewery on Southwest Boulevard, with hour-long tours ending in a tasting and a rooftop-view beer hall.
sights.hours: Beer hall 12:00–9:00 PM Mon–Thu, 11:00 AM–10:00 PM Fri–Sat, 10:00 AM–7:00 PM Sun; tours daily

sights.name: Kauffman Center for the Performing Arts
sights.note: Shell-shaped glass-and-steel concert hall by Moshe Safdie, home to the symphony, opera and ballet, overlooking the Crossroads.
sights.hours: Performance times; free public tours on select days

sights.name: Westport
sights.note: Kansas City's oldest neighbourhood turned bar-and-music strip around Westport Road and Pennsylvania Avenue; busiest late on weekends.
sights.hours: Bars and restaurants mostly to ~1:30–3:00 AM

sights.name: Loose Park
sights.note: Leafy Civil War battlefield turned park with a pond, walking loop and the Laura Conyers Smith rose garden, at its best in late spring.
sights.hours: Daily, early morning to late evening

railStations.name: Kansas City Union Station
railStations.note: Restored 1914 station at 30 W Pershing Road with Amtrak's daily Southwest Chief (Chicago–Los Angeles) and Missouri River Runner trains to St. Louis. The Union Station streetcar stop at Pershing & Main is a short walk, about 10 min by streetcar to downtown.
railStations.hours: Station building open daily; trains from early morning to late evening (Southwest Chief also in the late evening/early morning).

airports.name: Kansas City International Airport
airports.transitNote: No rail link and not on the map; the airport is ~25 km north of downtown. RideKC Route 229 (Boardwalk–KCI) runs about hourly between the terminal and downtown via the Boardwalk Square transit centre, ~1 hour for the regular $2 bus fare. A taxi or rideshare takes ~25–30 min.
airports.hours: Route 229 runs 7 days a week, roughly hourly from early morning to late evening; check ridekc.org.
